items.label: What it is
items.html: Not a country. A continent governed under the Antarctic Treaty. Most tourist voyages (98% in IAATO's 2025-26 figures) go to the Antarctic Peninsula region.

items.label: Where trips go
items.html: Antarctic Peninsula, South Shetland Islands, Weddell Sea, Ross Sea, and the sub-Antarctic: South Georgia and the Falklands.

items.label: Season
items.html: IAATO describes the Peninsula season as October to April. In 2024-25, landings ran from 22 October to 1 April. Month by month.

items.label: Departure ports
items.html: Ushuaia, Argentina, for most ship voyages; Punta Arenas, Chile, for flights to King George Island. Compare routes.

items.label: The crossing
items.html: The Drake Passage, about 850 km wide, lies between South America and the Antarctic Peninsula. Fly-cruises fly over it instead.

items.label: Landing limits
items.html: IAATO members may land no more than 100 visitors at one site at a time, and ships carrying more than 500 passengers may not land at all. Why ship size matters.

items.label: Visitors
items.html: 113,518 visitors with IAATO operators in the 2025-26 season (as of 10 April 2026), of whom 85,195 landed.
